subject.title: [RFC] Agent Teleconference — minimum-viable scoped meeting primitive with working prototype

question: Should OpenClaw accept a core meeting-lifecycle primitive for agent teleconference, and if so what storage/auth/transcript contract should it use?
rationale: The RFC spans core CLI, persisted state, transcript retention, cross-agent authorization, and config identity surfaces; those are product and security boundaries that source inspection cannot choose automatically.

options.title: Sponsor narrow core lifecycle after design
options.body: Approve a small core meeting lifecycle only after maintainers settle SQLite vs named artifact storage, transcript retention/redaction, authorization, and the temporary relationship to sessions_send/A2A.

options.title: Keep as plugin/API exploration
options.body: Ask the contributor to keep the prototype outside core until a missing plugin or SDK API is identified and solved with a smaller extension-point PR.

options.title: Fold into broader collaboration RFC
options.body: Defer this lifecycle primitive into the broader multi-agent collaboration roadmap tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/35203.

recommendation.title: Sponsor narrow core lifecycle after design
recommendation.body: Approve a small core meeting lifecycle only after maintainers settle SQLite vs named artifact storage, transcript retention/redaction, authorization, and the temporary relationship to sessions_send/A2A.
